label: copy-phase input b (fed-back b), from the 2nd copy output onward
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is b (i.e. the model just output b, an original b at position >= 1). It never fires during the original phase or at <DEL>, and essentially never on other input tokens. Magnitude grows with position in the copy: b copied at recall_idx 1 (original position 0) is weak/rare (rate ~0.3%), and activation rises with recall_idx, saturating around recall_idx >= 4 (~3.3% step rate overall; top activations are b at original positions 6-8). Repeated b at a later position also activates. Not modulated by out_tok, next_out or prev_tok. False positives are mainly b at early original positions (1-2) in the copy phase.

issues: I reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.838, R 0.978, F1 0.903, mass recall 0.994. The profile backs the main claims. Activation is zero in the original phase and at <DEL>. 63315 of 63419 active steps have in_tok b, with only about 100 scattered on q, k and others. in_first is never 1 when active, so the feature only fires on b's that are repeats or fed back.

The false positives follow a clear pattern, and the explanation already describes it. On dev, precision by recall_idx is: 1 -> 0.08, 2 -> 0.52, 3 -> 0.77, 4 -> 0.97, 5-8 -> about 0.99. So the false positives are fed-back b's from original positions 1-2. This looks like a ramp in strength (weak near-threshold activations early in the copy), not a missing condition. Of the test misses, 1382 steps hold only 0.6% of the activation mass, and most are r=1 (b at original position 0) with weak activations.

One claim overreaches: 'prev_tok does not change it' only holds overall. At recall_idx 2, precision varies with prev_tok from 0.33 (prev 3) and 0.36 (prev b) to 0.93 (prev c). In the weak early-copy region, the token before b moves the activation across the firing threshold. The pattern is spread across many tokens, so no compact predicate fixes it.

The phrase 'from the 2nd copy output onward' is slightly ambiguous. The predicate recall_idx >= 2 means the fed-back b is original position 1 or later, i.e. the second fed-back token. Read that way, it matches the predicate.

I found no better simple predicate. recall_idx >= 3 trades recall for precision (dev F1 0.88, as the other agent reported), and splitting further by L gives no clean cut. For example, precision at recall_idx 2 ranges from 0.27 to 0.64 across L with no monotone trend.
